---
title: 'barroso_add_char_template'
description: 'Append a blank morphological-character template to a species table.'
toc: true
toc-depth: 3
---


```{r}
#| eval: false
barRoso::barroso_add_char_template()
```

### Description

Given a `data.frame` of species (one row per species, or
per specimen) OR a path to an Excel file containing such data, this
function writes an `.xlsx` file whose columns begin with whatever
identification columns are in `species_df` — Genus/Species/Author,
Family/Taxon, etc. — and continue with a standard morphological-character
template (HABIT, STIPULE, LEAF, INFLORESCENCE, FLOWER, FRUIT, SEED) left
empty for the user to fill in.

When `plant_group` is specified, INFLORESCENCE/FLOWER/FRUIT blocks
are replaced with the morphology that group actually has — e.g.
Leguminosae-Papilionoideae swaps generic petals for STANDARD / WING /
KEEL and adds stamen arrangement and fruit dehiscence; Asteraceae
replaces the inflorescence with capitulum + involucre and the flower
block with RAY / DISC florets + pappus; Ochnaceae uses the full
carpophore/mericarp fruit and seed-apical-hook block; Orchidaceae uses
dorsal/lateral sepals, labellum and column. Supported groups:

- "Leguminosae-Papilionoideae"
- "Leguminosae-Caesalpinioideae"
- "Leguminosae-Mimosoideae"
- "Asteraceae"
- "Ochnaceae"
- "Orchidaceae"

The resulting file is the input format expected by
`barroso_write_taxon_descr()`: column-name conventions match
(capitalised group prefixes, lowercase subterms, "(cm)" / "(mm)" /
"(m)" units, "length" / "width" / "height" keywords).

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| species_df | Either a `data.frame` containing the species-identification columns you want preserved (e.g. Genus, Species, Author), OR a character string path to an Excel file (.xlsx) containing such data. Every column in `species_df` is copied into the output as-is; template columns are appended after them and written empty. Any template column whose name already exists in `species_df` is skipped, so user data is never overwritten. |
| sheet | Character string or integer. Sheet name or index to read when `species_df` is a path to an Excel file. Default is 1. |
| plant_group | Optional character. One of the supported profiles listed above. `NULL` (default) uses the generic flowering-plant profile. |
| species_cols | Character vector or integer indices. Column names or indices used to build the species header (e.g., c("Genus", "Species", "Author") or 1:3). These can be combined flexibly (e.g., a single "Scientific_name" column or separate Genus, Species, and Author columns). |
| overwrite | Logical. If TRUE (default), an existing file at the target path is overwritten; if FALSE, the function errors out. |
| format_excel | Logical. If TRUE (default), the function will use more user-friendly format for the spreadsheet. |
| sheet_name | Character. Name of the worksheet. Default "described_specimens". |
| base_font_size | Numeric. Base font size. Default 10. |
| base_font_name | Character. Base font name. Default "Calibri Light". |
| verbose | Logical. Print progress messages. Default TRUE. |
| filename | Output file base name (with or without ".xlsx"). If NULL, uses "taxon_template" or "<plant_group>_template" when a group is given. |
| dir | Output directory. If NULL, a directory named after `filename` (without extension) is created in the working directory. A date-stamped subfolder is created inside. |

### Value

Invisibly returns the absolute path to the written .xlsx file.

### Examples

```r
# Using a data frame
species_df <- data.frame(
  Genus   = c("Ouratea", "Ouratea", "Ouratea"),
  Species = c("acicularis", "acuminata", "cassinefolia"),
  Author  = c("R.G.Chacon & K.Yamam.", "(DC.) Engl.", "(DC.) Engl.")
)

barroso_add_char_template(
  species_df = species_df,
  filename   = "Ouratea_template"
)

# Using an Excel file path
barroso_add_char_template(
  species_df = "my_species_list.xlsx",
  sheet = 1,
  plant_group = "Ochnaceae",
  filename = "Ouratea_Ochnaceae_template"
)
```
